mt_nuggets_the.blurb: The Nuggets is a compact outcrop in the Revenue Flats desert country of southwest Montana, a short drive from Norris and roughly 5,600 feet up. Fourteen routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad climbs, cluster on one formation in the middle of a loop road. Grades sit in the lower and middle range: a couple of 5.6s and 5.8s, a handful of 5.9s, and the largest group at 5.10. The wall stands close to the road, so belaying from the car is possible. Some lines lack fixed anchors, which means walking around the back of the rock to get down. Expect company on warm spring days, which also makes it easy to find partners to share a rope with.

mt_headstrong_buttress.blurb: Headstrong Buttress is a granite crag above the highway south of Red Lodge, Montana, at about 7,250 feet. Routes are nearly all one pitch and combine crack and face climbing, so bring a rack as well as quickdraws for the bolted lines. The left side stands steep and vertical with a blend of bolts and gear, while the right side lies at a lower angle. A low-angled slab known as the School Room holds short bolted lines that suit beginners. The grade range stretches from easy 5.5s up through plenty of 5.10, with a few 5.11 and one 5.12 for stronger climbers. The hike up from the road is about a quarter hour.

mt_pit_stop.blurb: Pit Stop is a roadside crag on the west shore of Lake Koocanusa in far northwest Montana, the easiest-to-reach wall in the wider Koocanusa Crags group, and you can park right beside it. The rock is glacially polished quartzite and the face catches the morning sun. Thirteen climbs are split about evenly between bolted sport lines and trad routes, plus a single boulder problem. Most grades land at 5.10 and 5.11, with a few moderate 5.8 and 5.9 lines to warm up on and one 5.12 at the top end. Most routes earn two or three stars, and a four-star 5.9 is the standout.

mt_skyline_north.blurb: Skyline North is the north-facing side of Skyline Buttress, high on the east side of Gallatin Canyon near Bozeman at roughly 6,700 feet. It holds thirteen traditional routes on canyon gneiss, ranging from a long moderate 5.6 climb of six pitches through steady 5.9 to 5.11 lines and a couple of hard 5.12 and 5.13 test pieces. The north aspect and the altitude keep it cooler than most of the canyon in summer. Reaching it means a long uphill hike on the main climbers' trail beyond a lower formation, so allow plenty of time and start early. Several routes here earn four stars.

mt_b_o_buttress.blurb: B. O. Buttress sits on the east side of Gallatin Canyon near Bozeman, on the river-facing side, one formation over from The Waltz at around 5,700 feet. It is a single clean buttress with thirteen routes, almost all of them traditional, with a bolted line or two and some top-rope options. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, but the bulk sit between 5.9 and 5.11, with 5.11 the most common. The climbing is varied rather than one-note, which suits a party of mixed ability that wants trad at a range of levels. Plan on a hike in along the river trail from the highway.

mt_raspberry_boulder.blurb: Raspberry Boulder is a lone boulder in Hyalite Canyon near Bozeman, tucked across Hyalite Creek near the lower end of the road to the reservoir. It carries twelve problems, mostly easy to moderate: a handful in the V0 to V2 band, and a few harder ones topping out around V3 to V4. Forest surrounds it on every side, which blocks wind and makes for pleasant conditions on blustery days. The rock was cleaned when it was developed but can still be a bit dirty. Reaching it takes a short walk from the road and a shallow creek crossing, which can be tricky in snow or high water.

mt_first_buttress_2.blurb: First Buttress is a small, quiet crag on the east side of Gallatin Canyon outside Bozeman, reached by the river trail and sitting below the Blackline area at about 5,800 feet. Roughly a dozen routes cover mostly trad with a couple of bolted sport lines and a few top-rope options. The range is wide for a small wall: a pair of 5.8s, a few at 5.10, then a run of 5.12 and a few 5.13 test pieces for strong climbers. The rock is serviceable rather than superb, and traffic stays light compared with the bigger buttresses nearby, so it works well for people wanting a mix of moderate trad and hard projects.

mt_carwash_the.blurb: The Carwash is a newer sector of Stone Hill on the west side of Lake Koocanusa in northwest Montana, with routes put up from 2020 onward. Walls face east and sit under a tree canopy, so most of the climbing stays shaded, with full shade by late afternoon. Twelve routes mix sport and trad, with some top-rope lines. Grades start at 5.8, but the bulk are 5.10 to 5.11, and several sit around 5.12, so this is better for intermediate and strong climbers than for novices. The trail up to the base is short and pleasant, and belay ledges are comfortable.
